title: The SSF conformance PR added GET/PATCH/PUT stream handlers plus stream verify and status views without the add_stream provider permission check that the existing POST handler enforces, so any token holder for the app can read, modify, verify and disable its event streams.

findings.explanation: All database queries use Django ORM with parameterized lookups. No raw SQL or string interpolation into queries is present in this diff.

The SSFStreamViewSet is changed from ReadOnlyModelViewSet to include DestroyModelMixin, adding a DELETE endpoint. The queryset is 'Stream.objects.all()' with no visible ownership/permission filtering beyond whatever the base GenericViewSet provides. There is no explicit permission_classes, filter_backends, or get_queryset override shown in the diff that would restrict deletion to only streams belonging to the authenticated user/tenant. This could allow any authenticated user to delete any stream (IDOR via CWE-639 or missing authorization via CWE-862). The authentication/authorization may be handled elsewhere in the codebase (e.g., a base class or router-level permission), but it is not visible in this diff.

evidence.content:
class SSFStreamViewSet(
    mixins.RetrieveModelMixin,
    mixins.DestroyModelMixin,
    mixins.ListModelMixin,
    GenericViewSet,
):
    """SSFStream Viewset"""

    queryset = Stream.objects.all()

findings.suggested_fix: Ensure that permission_classes are set appropriately on SSFStreamViewSet and that get_queryset() filters streams to only those belonging to the current user/application. For example, override get_queryset to filter by the provider's backchannel_application accessible to the requesting user, and add an ownership check before destroy.
